items.title: The cyclotomic KLR quotient at a dominant integral weight
items.strategy: The idempotents isolate the individual generators, so the displayed ideal also equals $R(\beta)a(x_1)R(\beta)$ when the latter expression is restricted to this block. In the standard choice each isolated generator is homogeneous; this proves the grading, without falsely assigning one degree to their sum. Over a degree-zero field a monic homogeneous polynomial of positive dot degree is the pure power. Lower monic coefficients therefore require forgetting the grading. The example $\lambda_i=2$, $a_i=u(u-1)$ gives $k\oplus k$ at root $\alpha_i$, so its two projective classes cannot be the one-dimensional middle weight of $V(2)$; the standard graded hypothesis is substantive. The rank-zero convention avoids an undefined first letter of the empty word. This definition uses no choice.

items.title: The minimal-parabolic KLR diagram proof category
items.statement:
Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots, a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and admissible weighted-homogeneous KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. Write $b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$ and fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear category of weighted oriented diagrams with objects weights, downward generators $G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$ for every $j$, and the single upward generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums and grading shifts; use idempotent completion when speaking of word projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes normalized projective restriction: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h$, it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by $-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$. The native crossing is $\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference $(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put $\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$. Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR relations of the cited Definition.

At input $i$-weight $h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$, the first unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree $d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and second unit $1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$ prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix $H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\}$; for $h<0$ prescribe $G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}$. The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap transfer, and the identity columns/rows are the indicated dotted units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse equations; the dotted dual rows/columns are the finite triangular coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$, if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and $p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion/projection with product $1_{H_iG_i}$.

The normalized far-left bubble series $A_\mu(t),\mathsf H_\mu(t)$ have constant coefficient1 and satisfy $A_\mu(t)\mathsf H_\mu(t)=1$. Genuine negative-degree bubbles vanish. The $A$ coefficient with index $m$ is the clockwise bubble with $-h-1+m$ dots when this count is nonnegative, extended by formal inverse coefficients otherwise; its degree is $2d_i m$. The other family has dot count $h-1+\ell$ and degree $2d_i\ell$. Impose the finite-coefficient slides verified on the monic flag model: adjoining an $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$ and multiplies $\mathsf H$ by that factor; adjoining a spectator root $y$ of color $j\ne i$ multiplies $A$ by $q_{ij}^{\rm rev}(y,t)=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}$ is the nonzero extremal coefficient, and divides $\mathsf H$ by it. Every reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant coefficient1.

Impose the rank-one cross-and-cap equations: the two oppositely oriented single-crossing curls are the signed sums of a dotted uncrossed cap and an opposite bubble over indices $a+b=-1$; the two opposite-crossing cancellations are the straight pair plus the dotted cup--bubble--cap sums over $a+b+c=-1$, with the corresponding opposite-orientation signs. A negative dot count on an open strand is zero. These are the four source $\kappa$ equations, converted globally by $\kappa=-\tau$. For $j\ne i$, the two sideways crossings, defined as the two adjunction mates of the downward crossing, cancel in the two orders with the nonzero scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$; scale the reverse mate by the corresponding inverse to obtain the mixed isomorphism $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$, commuting with the $j$ dot. These are relations of this proof-tool category. Their consistency and homogeneous realization are established by the polynomial flag model, rather than assumed for the actual cyclotomic induction/restriction action.
items.strategy: This is a presentation by generators and homogeneous equations. Check weighted homogeneity of every downward relation using $\deg x_j=2d_j$ and $\deg\tau_{jk}=-b_{jk}$; the global source substitution changes every crossing sign and preserves $Q$. Check the two cup/cap degrees at adjacent weights, giving degree-zero triangle composites and the symmetric identity shifts in both branches of the rank-one matrix. Interpret all fake bubbles and reciprocal slide coefficients by the finite recursion from constant coefficient1, so no analytic series or inverse dot occurs. The local polynomial flag model realizes these equations with normalized $H_i$, shifted spectator flags, explicit dual monic power bases and the actual rank-one inverse blocks, proving consistency. This last well-definedness result is listed in justified_by, while its proof depends on the present definition; it is not a logical dependency of the definition.

items.title: Mixed relations, local nilpotence and weights give the integrable quantum action
items.statement: Let $V=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}V_\mu$ be a label-weight-graded $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with its toral operators, and operators $E_i,F_i$ of weights $\alpha_i,-\alpha_i$. Assume the toral conjugation and mixed relations, and local nilpotence of each $E_i,F_i$; vectors have finite label support. Then these operators uniquely define an integrable type-one $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module for EVERY real symmetrizable datum. Every vector has a finite rank-one $U_i$ orbit and the admissible Kashiwara $i$-string decomposition applies. Finite weight spaces do not imply finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ orbits; no such conclusion is asserted.
items.strategy: Apply the exact general supplier [[lem-integrable-rank-one-actions-force-the-quantum-serre-relations]], or reproduce its argument as follows. Rank-one PBW writes the orbit of $v$ as $F_i^aE_i^bK_i^cv$; only finitely many $b$ and then finitely many $a$ survive, so $W=U_iv$ is finite. For $j\ne i$, $W'=U_i(F_jW)$ is also finite. In $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ the Hopf adjoint actions are $\operatorname{ad}E_i(T)=(E_iT-TE_i)K_i$ and $\operatorname{ad}F_i(T)=F_iT-K_iTK_i^{-1}F_i$. The map $T=F_j$ is highest of rank-one weight $m=-a_{ij}\ge0$. The finite quantum-sl2 string theorem gives $(\operatorname{ad}F_i)^{m+1}T=0$. Expanding yields $\sum_{r=0}^{n}(-1)^r q_i^{r(m-n+1)}{n\brack r}_i F_i^{n-r}TF_i^r$; at $n=m+1$ every Laurent exponent is zero, precisely the negative Serre relation. Exchange $E,F,K$ with $F,E,K^{-1}$ for positive Serre. Thus every defining relation holds, with no A2 calculation, rank-two local-finiteness assumption or presupposed quantum module. Uniqueness follows from generators; local nilpotence gives integrability.

items.title: Cyclotomic induction and restriction functors
items.statement: Use the standard graded quotient of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]. Put $A=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $B=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ and $e=e(\beta,i)$. Right append defines a graded CORNER homomorphism $\iota_i:A\to eBe$, sending $1_A$ to $e$, $e(\nu)$ to $e(\nu i)$, and the old dots/crossings to their positions in the first $|\beta|$ strands. It is not asserted injective and $e$ may be zero. Define $F_i^{\rm basic}(M)=Be\otimes_A M$ and $E_i^{\rm basic}(N)=eN$. These additive functors preserve shifts and satisfy $F_i^{\rm basic}\dashv E_i^{\rm basic}$ by degree-zero tensor-Hom evaluation. $F_i$ increases ROOT degree by $\alpha_i$ and decreases module weight $\Lambda-\beta$ by $\alpha_i$; restriction does the reverse. Both composites are endofunctors at a fixed root degree. The same underlying definitions apply ungraded to monic deformations. Exactness/projective preservation and the shifted second adjunction are theorems below.
items.strategy: Each generic generator relation is preserved in the corner, and the first-strand cyclotomic generator maps into the longer ideal. This gives a homomorphism with unit image $e$, not a global-unit inclusion. For example $\lambda_i=1$, $\beta=\alpha_i$ has $A=k$, $B=0$, so the corner homomorphism and induction are zero. Evaluation at $e$ identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(Be,N)$ with $eN$, proving the ordinary adjunction with its actual grading. Finite balanced tensors give additivity/shift compatibility. No unshifted second adjunction is assumed; its explicit shift is supplied by the coherent-adjunction lemma.

items.title: Cyclotomic dot annihilators, finite-dimensional blocks, and finite root strings
items.statement: Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)–(Q4) for a real symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree $\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the resulting ordinary quotient. Every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic annihilator in each fixed block, every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over $k$, and, for fixed $\beta,i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.
items.strategy:
Use the exact native presentation, and abbreviate its globally opposite source crossing by $\kappa_a=-\tau_a$ for every color pair; the dots, idempotents and $Q$ do not change. For equal adjacent colors put $x=x_a,y=x_{a+1}$ and $\partial f=(s_af-f)/(x-y)$. If $fe(\nu)$ annihilates a module, the source nil-Hecke identities give $(x-y)\kappa_a f\kappa_a e(\nu)=(s_af-f)\kappa_a e(\nu)=(\kappa_af-\partial f-f\kappa_a)e(\nu)$. The terms containing $f$ vanish, so $\partial f$ vanishes; then $s_af=f+(x-y)\partial f$ also vanishes. This proves annihilator closure under the divided difference and exchange without division by an integer. A common monic annihilator of the first dot is $g_1=\prod_j a_j$, with the zero corners understood in the same way.

Suppose a common monic $g$ of degree $d$ annihilates $x_a$. Equal-color exchange gives $g(y)=0$. At an unequal pair $j,l$, $\kappa_ag(x)\kappa_a=g(y)Q_{jl}(x,y)=0$. Set $C=k[x]/g$, finite free of rank $d$. Multiplication by $Q_{jl}(x,y)$ on $C[y]$ has matrix $M(y)$ with leading coefficient $c\,\mathrm{Id}$ and degree $-a_{lj}$ in $y$, where $c=t_{j,l;0,-a_{lj}}\ne0$. Its determinant $r(y)$ has leading coefficient $c^d$. Applying $\operatorname{adj}(M)M=r\,\mathrm{Id}$ to the vector $1$ gives $Q_{jl}(x,y)R(x,y)\equiv r(y)\pmod {g(x)}$. Thus $g(y)r(y)$ annihilates the corner; divide its leading scalar to obtain a monic polynomial. If $d=0$ that corner is zero; if $a_{lj}=0$, $r=c^d$ is a unit. Take the product over the finite words/pairs and induct over positions. PBW then reduces each dot exponent below its monic bound, leaving finitely many permutations, words and exponent tuples, so the block is finite dimensional. This is a direct ordinary-algebra argument for arbitrary monic polynomials, including $u(u-1)$, rather than a flat-specialization claim.

For standard powers one can strengthen the bounds to nilpotence. If $x^N=0$ and the neighboring colors differ, write $Q_{jl}(x,y)=c y^q+xH(x,y)$, $q=-a_{lj}$, using homogeneity and Q4. The quadratic relation gives $y^NQ=0$, hence $y^{N+q}=-c^{-1}xy^NH$ on the corner. Raising this commuting-polynomial equality to the $N$th power gives $y^{N(N+q)}=0$. Equal-color exchange preserves the exponent $N$. Starting with a common first-strand power proves nilpotence of every dot.

For finite root strings in either branch fix a prefix length $\ell$ and a common monic annihilator $g$ of degree $d$ for $x_{\ell+1}$ in the finite length-$\ell+1$ quotient. Its image annihilates that dot in every longer quotient, since right concatenation preserves the first-strand ideal. In an all-$i$ tail of length $d+1$ starting at position $\ell+1$, repeated annihilator closure gives $\partial_{\ell+d}\cdots\partial_{\ell+1}g(x_{\ell+1})=(-1)^d$, so the tail is zero. Equivalently, in native nil-Hecke rank $s>d$, multiply $g(x_1)$ by $x_1^{s-1-d}x_2^{s-2}\cdots x_{s-1}$. Its top term is the Artin staircase and its lower terms have smaller total degree; the native $\partial_{w_0}$ sends it to $1$. Thus $\partial_{w_0}$ and the full staircase idempotent belong to the ideal generated by $g$. The finite matrix units from the perfect Artin pairing put $1$ in that ideal. Both computations use unit diagonal elimination, never $s!^{-1}$.

Finally induct on the number $b$ of non-$i$ entries. Let $k=L_{b-1}$ be the previous bound and $\ell=b-1+k$. Choose an all-$i$ tail bound $m$ at that prefix length and set $L_b=k+m-1$. A word of length $b+L_b=\ell+m$ with at least $L_b$ copies of $i$ either has at least $k$ in its first $\ell$ positions, whose prefix is already zero, or has at most $k-1$ there and therefore all last $m$ positions are $i$. That tail is zero. A longer word with at most $b$ other colors has a zero initial segment of length $b+L_b$. For fixed $\beta$, $b=\sum_{j\ne i}\beta_j$, so $\beta_i+m\ge L_b$ kills every word in $\beta+m\alpha_i$. The prefix never has to end in color $i$. All constructions involve finite products, determinants, polynomial reductions and integer choices.

items.title: Generic KLR induction and restriction mixed relations and the rank-one exact sequence
items.strategy: Use the full labelled PBW shuffle decomposition, with word-idempotent shifts rather than a common graded-free shift. Same-end multiplication $x\otimes y\mapsto x\kappa_n y$, where $\kappa=-\tau_{native}$ on ALL color pairs, identifies the nonidentity cosets and gives $E_iF_j=q^{-b_{ij}}F_jE_i$ for unequal colors and $E_iF_i=q_i^{-2}F_iE_i\oplus\operatorname{Id}[t]$. For the opposite ends the overlap multiplication has image all transfer cosets except $\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_1$; taking that coefficient gives the cokernel $q^{-(\alpha_i,\beta)}M[t]$. Its middle functor is $E_i\bar F_i$, not $E_iF_i$. The PBW sequence is split on the right before tensoring, so no flatness of a quotient is assumed. Source/native minus signs merely multiply each chosen transfer basis by its explicit unit; the full presentation dictionary preserves Q and grading.

items.title: The minimal-parabolic polynomial flag model realizes the graded diagram relations
items.statement:
Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR parameters of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], PBW convention of [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the following polynomial flag construction realizes all the defining graded diagram relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap, bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic quotient identification.

Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets $Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$), put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$, $r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$, $t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$, $q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of degree $\lambda_i$. Initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous degrees, so all formulas are graded; the standard specialization is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r.$$
Let $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$: equivalently it is $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$. It is finite free over $C$, of rank $\binom Nr$, and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is $B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over $L_{m+i}$, with target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to $Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

Every downward generator carries the ordered shift
$$s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell.$$
Thus $G_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the $B_m\{-2d_ir\}$ tensor functor; $G_j$ for $j\ne i$ is the $C_m^j\{s_j(m)\}$ tensor functor. The basic reversed $i$ flag is $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}=B_m\otimes_{L_{m+i}}-$ without a shift, whereas the formal upward generator at INPUT vertex $m$ is
$$H_i(m)=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}.$$
These are distinct conventions. The basic flags have degree-zero $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\{t_i(m)\}\dashv F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$, where $t_i(m)=-2d_i(h_m-1)$. At vertex $m$ the formal first unit and second cap have degree $d_i(1-h_m)$, and the formal first cap and second unit have degree $d_i(1+h_m)$.

All four maps are explicit dual-basis maps of the two monic coefficient forms on $B_m$: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}:B_m\to L_m$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$; $\tau_{\mathrm{new}}:B_m\to L_{m+i}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$. The first cap is $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto\tau_{\mathrm{new}}(b_1b_2)$ and first cup is its dual-power-basis Casimir; the second cap/cup use $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$. For a monic polynomial $f$ their Casimir is the polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the two-root quotient.

Source crossings are $\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for EVERY color pair. Source equal-color operators are $(s-1)/(X-Y)$; source unequal operators are the switch/quotient in the increasing-color direction and switch times $Q$ in the reverse direction. Thus native operators are their negatives, and both actual crossing degrees are $-b_{jk}$ with the ordered shifts above. On the $i,j$ pair the successive underlying rings are $D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, with source maps $\pi:D_1\to D_0$ and $f\mapsto Q_{ij}(z,y)f:D_0\to D_1$. Their normalized opposite-sideways composites have scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$; in the NE/SW-$i$, NW/SE-$j$ source orientation the double-mate ratio is $t_{ji}/t_{ij}$. Native minus signs leave the two-crossing scalars and ratio unchanged. Basic $E_iG_j\cong(G_jE_i)\{-b_{ij}\}$; normalized formal $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$ is unshifted.

The canonical rank-one $\rho$ and its inverse, the same-color cross/cap equations, the bubble series $\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ and its reciprocal, and the finite coefficient bubble-slide identities are realized by the stated polynomial maps. In particular the normalized positive $h$ identity columns have degrees $d_i(1-h+2k)$ for $0\le k<h$, and the negative branch uses the inverse crossing plus the dot/cap rows. All polynomial pairings and relations persist after arbitrary monic coefficient specialization as UNGRADED identities. Such a specialization does not assert nilpotence, a homogeneous trace degree, or a highest-weight $K_0$ claim. No geometry, characteristic restriction, or one-dimensional-Hom hypothesis is imposed.
items.strategy:
Work entirely with the displayed formal-model rings and operators; neither a generic cyclotomic Frobenius theorem nor an actual quotient/faithfulness result is an input. The following is the full local construction route.

(1) Monic splitting algebras and nil-Hecke matrix units. Over the universal coefficient ring S=k[c_1,...,c_N], repeatedly adjoin a root of the monic framing polynomial and divide it out. At the s-th step the residual polynomial is monic of the next smaller degree, so ordinary monic division gives the Artin basis X_1^{a_1}...X_N^{a_N}, 0<=a_j<=N-j. For a monic extension D[z]/f of degree q the top-coefficient pairing has Gram entries zero for a+b<q-1 and one for a+b=q-1; reversing one basis makes it triangular with diagonal1. Hence its pairing is perfect over every coefficient ring, with no factorial division. Composing these forms gives the normalized Artin divided-difference form (-1)^{ell(w_N)}kappa_{w_N}. Its staircase value is1 and every other Artin basis monomial has lower degree. If u_a,v_a are dual Artin bases, f -> u_a delta(v_b f) are matrix units in NH_r; PBW leading-permutation independence makes the polynomial representation injective, so NH_r=End_{Sym_r}(Pol_r). This proves the required graded nil-Hecke matrix algebra directly.

Block monic splitting makes Pol_N free of rank r!(N-r)! over T_r=Sym_r tensor Sym_{N-r}. The parabolic divided-difference form T_r->S composes with the perfect block Artin form to the perfect Pol_N/S form. Tensoring its pairing map with the nonzero free T_r-module Pol_N therefore gives an isomorphism; faithful-flat descent proves the T_r pairing perfect. T_r is finite graded projective over S by the explicit block-staircase retraction; lift a homogeneous basis modulo S_+, split the resulting finite free surjection, and use graded Nakayama on its kernel to prove T_r graded free. Its rank is N!/[r!(N-r)!]. This proves the claimed L_m rank after arbitrary monic basechange. Matrix trace composed with the parabolic form gives the model's cyclic perfect form; this is a proved polynomial-model pairing, not the theorem about the generic KLR algebra.

To identify the monic quotient without an external Grassmannian theorem, represent NH_r as the full matrix algebra on its Artin module. The entries of multiplication by a monic p(X_1) generate exactly the coefficients of the remainder of p(u) modulo c_r(u): the first matrix column contains them, while every other entry is their polynomial combination. Matrix units show its two-sided matrix ideal is the ideal of those entries. Monic division makes those coefficients a unit triangular change from the consecutive complete-symmetric/factorization relations. Thus NH_r/(p(X_1)) is the matrix algebra over the stated monic factor ring. This also gives zero when r>N.

(2) Actual maps and their four triangles. B_m is the two monic root extensions described in the Statement. For f monic, the polynomial K_f(X,Y) is well defined before passing to f(X)=f(Y)=0. It satisfies (X-Y)K_f=0 and tau_X K_f=1. Thus tau_X(X^a K_f)=Y^a for every a, proving that K_f is precisely the dual-power-basis Casimir, not an unspecified inverse Gram matrix. The two Casimirs for b_{N-r} and c_{r+1} give the four displayed cups/caps. Their contractions are the two equalities sum v_a tau(z^a b)=b and sum tau(bv_a)z^a=b; substituting them in the tensor composites proves both triangles for each adjunction. The first maps have degree0 after the B{-2d_i r} shift. The second cap has degree -2d_i(N-r-1)+2d_i r=-2d_i(h-1); its unit has the opposite degree. Restoring normalized H at its input weight gives exactly the four formal degrees in the Statement. This proves the gradings as well as the underlying adjunctions.

(3) Rank-one rho and its finite block inverses. Use the PBW two-coset splitting for one extra i strand: the transfer term is a kappa_r b, and its polynomial complement is the new-dot algebra. The rank-one intertwiner is g=(u-X)-(u-X)^2 kappa. Its quadratic and dot-commutation identities follow by expanding kappa X_{r+1}-X_r kappa=1 and kappa^2=0. Multiply these intertwiners along the extra strand, and multiply the other transfer by p(X_1). Projecting to the PBW polynomial complement gives, with S_r(u)=product_{a<=r}(u-X_a)^2, a coefficient map A satisfying A(u^k S_r)=(-1)^r u^k p(u). The same mixed relation gives phi_{k+1}=u phi_k+E(psi_k), psi_{k+1}=psi_k X_r. Therefore A(u^k)=(-1)^r quo_{S_r}(u^k p): subtracting its product by S_r leaves degree below2r, and uniqueness of monic division proves the assertion. This is the explicit rank-one PBW calculation; it uses no cyclotomic commutator theorem as a supplier.

If h=N-2r>=0, these quotient polynomials have distinct leading degrees h+k and unit leading coefficient (-1)^r. They give an injective A and a unique polynomial remainder of degree<h. The actual rho is consequently (transfer, dot^k unit) from FE{-2d_i} plus the h identity columns to EF; its inverse takes that remainder, subtracts its section, and inverts the transfer on the kernel. If h=-q<=0, A is surjective and its kernel is the span of1,u,...,u^{q-1}. Its connecting-map images have dot/cap matrix with zero entries below the anti-diagonal and unit (-1)^r on the anti-diagonal, because the displayed recurrence has phi_0=...=phi_{q-1}=0 and phi_q=(-1)^r. Reversing rows and solving successively gives the actual negative rho inverse. These are finite polynomial block inverses. On regular Artin generators the same constructions give the H_r(N) model Mackey maps (a tensor b)->a kappa_r b and the dot/cap rows; the graded matrix-Morita identification gives their flag versions. The normalized formal H changes the positive identity shifts to d_i(1-h+2k); the negative dot/cap shifts change by the same input-weight rule. This verifies every rho map and inverse in the formal model.

(4) Same-color crossing/cap identities and bubbles. Equal crossings act by kappa=(s-1)/(X-Y), so kappa^2=0, the braid relation and the two mixed dot equations follow by the rational-polynomial divided-difference expansion. Since K_f is symmetric, its divided-difference correction is0; (X-Y)K_f=0 gives the dot-mate equations. Contracting a crossing against either Casimir and using the rho block inverse just computed produces the cross-and-cap/curl equations: equivalently expand (f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y) in the power bases and take the top-coefficient rows. This is a finite polynomial computation, with the coefficient of each basis vector supplied by the same monic-division remainder; its first two curl forms are the signed sum x^a B_b over a+b=-1, and the two double-curl forms are the identity term plus the sums over a+b+c=-1. Negative dots on an open strand give0; fake bubbles are the corresponding inverse-series coefficients. Thus these equations are verified by the actual Casimir/rho maps rather than imposed on an unknown actual quotient.

At vertexm the resulting oriented bubble Laurent series is Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2, of leading degree h=N-2r. The opposite series is its normalized reciprocal; their product is1, coefficient by coefficient. This rational expression is forced by composing the two flag coefficient pairings: each existing i root contributes two factors, one from each side of the cap. Appending an i root z changes Phi to Phi/(u-z)^2, and appending a spectator j root y changes Phi to Phi Q_ij(u,y)/t_ij. Expanding these identities at infinity gives every finite bubble-slide coefficient equation. All coefficients use only additions, multiplication and monic formal inversion; there is no inverse of2 or of a factorial. These are the bubble-slide relations required in the formal proof-category definition. At an initial monic vacuum, closing a_i(x)x^{ell-1}=0 gives h_ell+sum c_{lambda-j}h_{ell-j}=0, h_0=1,h_<0=0, so H(t)a_i^rev(t)=1; the opposite series is a_i^rev. This also fixes the standard and deformed vacuum dictionaries without assuming quotient faithfulness.

(5) Downward Q relations and exact word grading. Give every flag the shift s_j(m) in the Statement. For j<k the increasing word(j,k) has a quotient/switch of underlying degree0 to word(k,j), whose target-unit minus source-unit shift is -b_jk. The reverse operator has underlying degree -2b_jk and unit-shift difference +b_jk. Both therefore have actual degree -b_jk; same-color divided differences have degree -2d_j. Native operators are all their negatives, so their degrees and two-crossing composites are unchanged. The ordinary polynomial operators verify idempotents, dots, far commutativity and Q quadratics directly. Expanding a three-strand composition gives zero difference when outer colors differ, and the divided difference of Q when they agree, exactly the source braid numerator. Global kappa=-tau changes all cubic signs and gives the actual native numerator. Quotient relations descend: on an i,j pair D_1 has bq=0 and D_0 has b=0; Qb=t_ij bq makes multiplication byQ well defined, and the other crossing is the literal quotient. The same identities with other spectator flags are just the polynomial-representation identities on appended alphabets.

(6) Mixed cups/caps and their exact leading constants. In D[z]/p versus D[z]/(pq), the coefficient form obeys tau_{pq}(Q f)=t_ij tau_p(f) because Q=t_ij q and the leading coefficient of Q f is t_ij times that of f. For a full existing i string use the ordered residue form of the model H_r(p): t_r^p(z)=(-1)^{r(N-r)} Res(Delta_r(X) X_1^{r-1}...X_{r-1} Tr(z)/product p(X_a)). No1/r! occurs. Expand parabolic divided differences to verify this over the universal integral coefficient ring; in its rational generic-root fraction field, the sum over root orderings is the Vandermonde determinant, so its two Vandermonde factors cancel the internal root-difference denominator. Both sides are integral polynomial expressions, hence the identity specializes to every field. With p'=p q and U_r=product Q_ij(X_a,y), cancellation gives t_r^{p'}(U_r z)=(-1)^{r A_ij}t_ij^r t_r^p(z). Perfectness of the model forms makes U_r on the old quotient injective. Testing the relative cap against these forms then gives pi_r epsilon_r^{p'}(Q(X_{r+1},y) lift(z))=(-1)^{A_ij}t_ij epsilon_r^p(z) for every nil-Hecke coset element, not only dot polynomials. Normalize the second maps by the global weight sign (-1)^{h+1}; N and h have the same parity, and the new N changes by A_ij, so the displayed sign cancels and the constant is precisely t_ij. Dual-power-basis contraction gives the mixed-unit equation. Reversing colors gives t_ji, and their quotient is the stated double-mate ratio. Native minus signs occur twice in these composites, so the scalars persist. No dimension-one Hom inference is used.

Finally, basic E_iG_j and G_jE_i have unit-shift difference b_ij, giving the stated basic shifted isomorphism. For normalized H the two unit sums are s_j(m)-d_i(1+h_m+A_ij) and -d_i(1+h_m)+s_j(m-e_i); they are equal because s_j(m-e_i)=s_j(m)+b_ij and b_ij=-d_i A_ij. This verifies the formal unshifted mixed commutator and its grading. All the defining relations have now been realized on the explicit flag modules. Monic extensions, their Casimirs, finite rho inverses and coefficient identities survive arbitrary monic specialization as ungraded maps. This lemma proves only the formal MODEL relations; its subsequent faithfulness and cyclotomic word-corner transfer belong to separate suppliers, and no generic trace, K_0 or crystal result is used. The construction is choice-free.

items.title: One-step KLR simple restriction, induction, and the first-dot index
items.statement: Let k be any field and R(Q) the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable Cartan datum and any homogeneous Q satisfying the standing symmetry and nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared up to internal shift. For a simple S of root weight beta and r=epsilon_i(S)>0, its ordinary one-step last-i restriction has a single simple graded socle and a single simple graded head, each once and of the same shift orbit, with epsilon_i=r-1; its maximum-epsilon composition part has coefficient a grading shift of [r]_i. The last-dot nilpotence index on that restriction is exactly r. The first-end statements hold with epsilon_i^L and the first dot. For every n>=1, Ind(S boxtimes L(i^n)) has a unique simple graded head f_i^n S, occurring once in its whole composition series, with epsilon_i=r+n (also when r=0); all other constituents have smaller epsilon_i. One-step simple socle and simple induction head are partial inverses. A simple S survives the first-strand cyclotomic quotient with exponents lambda_i exactly when epsilon_i^L(S)<=lambda_i for all i. Right restriction preserves surviving simples, while projected right induction has the same simple head when that generic head survives and is zero otherwise. These are shift-orbit assertions and do not assert factorial socle multiplicity.
items.strategy:
## Nil-Hecke branching computation

Let L_r be the nil-Hecke simple, modeled by the coinvariant algebra C_r=k[t_1,...,t_r]/(e_1,...,e_r) with polynomial multiplication and divided differences. Put z=t_r, and write E_a for elementary symmetric polynomials in t_1,...,t_(r-1). The equations e_a=E_a+z E_(a-1)=0 give E_a=(-z)^a for 1<=a<=r-1, and the final equation gives z^r=0. Consequently

    C_r = k[t_1,...,t_(r-1)] tensor_(k[E_1,...,E_(r-1)]) k[z]/(z^r),

where E_a acts on the second factor by (-z)^a. This is an equality of presented algebras, not a dimension heuristic. The polynomial representation of NH_(r-1) is a free module of rank (r-1)! over its symmetric center and identifies NH_(r-1) with the full matrix algebra over that center. After this specialization its image on C_r is Mat_((r-1)!)(k[z]/(z^r)), and C_r is its standard column module. Thus its graded socle and head are each one shifted L_(r-1), its simple composition coefficient is a shifted [r]_i, and multiplication by z has nilpotence index exactly r. The simple socle is the column over z^(r-1)k, the head the column modulo z. For r=1 this is the statement C_1=k and z=0. The same calculation with the first variable distinguished gives first-end branching. Matrix units and a monic Artin polynomial basis make the computation valid in all characteristics.

The induction NH_r tensor NH_n -> NH_(r+n) of L_r tensor L_n is L_(r+n), up to shift. Every positive full symmetric polynomial acts by zero, since its coproduct is a sum of products of block symmetric polynomials with at least one positive factor. Hence the induced module is a module over the full nil-Hecke central matrix quotient. PBW freeness computes its dimension as binomial(r+n,r)r!n!=(r+n)!, exactly the standard column dimension; it is therefore one simple column, not a factorial number of simples.

## Restriction has a simple socle

Let S have epsilon_i(S)=r>0. The maximum possible epsilon_i of a composition factor of e_i S is r-1 by the exact defining corners. Let U be any simple subobject of e_i S, and put t=epsilon_i(U). The final dot z commutes with R(beta-alpha_i) and acts nilpotently on e_i S: this holds on the whole S by positive dot degree and finite grading support. It preserves the socle and its ungraded isotypic components. On the isotypic component containing U, a suitable nonzero power image has a nonzero kernel copy of the same underlying simple type, killed by z. Absolute simplicity and the finite graded semisimple decomposition let one choose that copy homogeneously, with the appropriate shift. The induction–restriction adjunction therefore gives a nonzero map Ind(U,L_1)->S, hence a surjection. The graded shuffle formula bounds every induced tail by t+1, so r<=t+1. The preceding upper bound gives t=r-1.

Now apply the maximal (r-1)-tail corner p to e_i S, retaining R(beta-r alpha_i) tensor NH_(r-1). Original10 gives Delta_i^r S=N tensor L_r, with epsilon_i(N)=0. Hence

    p(e_i S)=N tensor Res_(NH_(r-1))L_r.

The right side has a single simple socle by the nil-Hecke computation and the absolute simplicity of N. Every simple subobject U of e_i S has t=r-1, so original10 makes pU a nonzero simple object. Exactness of p makes p(soc e_i S) semisimple and injects it into the one-simple socle of p(e_i S). Thus soc e_i S is itself a single simple object, once, with epsilon r-1. This also proves detection: any nonzero submodule of e_i S contains a simple graded submodule U, whose pU is nonzero.

## Simple head and global dot index

Finite graded psi-duality D is exact, takes simples to simples, fixes the corner idempotents and commutes with restriction; it needs no self-dual representative. Apply the socle proof to DS, whose epsilon equals r, and dualize. It follows that e_i S has a single simple head, once. The maximum-tail restriction of the head and socle have the same first factor N up to the corresponding duals and grading shifts: the nil-Hecke head/socle differ only by shift. Original10's unique-head recursion therefore identifies their shift orbits.

On p(e_i S), z^r=0 while z^(r-1)!=0 by the explicit nil-Hecke model. The image of z^r on all of e_i S is a graded submodule. Its p-corner is zero; the just-proved detection property forces that image to be zero. Nonvanishing of z^(r-1) in the p-corner implies its nonvanishing globally. Therefore the last-dot nilpotence index on e_i S is exactly r. Repeating the proof for the first-end maximal restriction gives first-dot nilpotence index exactly epsilon_i^L(S). Notice that this argument uses detection of all submodules; knowing the index only on the maximal corner would not suffice on its own.

## Nonreduced induction and partial inverses

Put M_n=Ind(S,L_n), n>=1. Its maximum tail is at most r+n by shuffle. At tail r+n the Mackey filtration can only retain all n added i-strands and precisely r original terminal i-strands: taking fewer added strands would require more than r from S, while taking fewer original strands would not fill the requested tail. Thus the maximum corner is

    Delta_i^(r+n)M_n = N tensor Ind_(NH_r tensor NH_n)^(NH_(r+n))(L_r tensor L_n)
                      = N tensor L_(r+n),

up to the fixed grading shift. This is one actual surviving filtration term and is simple.

Every simple quotient T of M_n has that maximum tail. Indeed adjunction gives a nonzero injection S tensor L_n -> Delta_i^n T. Restrict its first factor to S's maximal r-tail; the resulting nonzero corner implies epsilon_i(T)>=r+n. The shuffle bound gives equality. The finite semisimple head of M_n therefore has only constituents detected by its simple maximum corner; exactness implies that head is one simple constituent, once. Its maximum corner is the displayed simple module. The kernel of M_n->hd M_n has zero maximum corner, so every other composition factor has smaller epsilon and the head occurs once in the entire composition series.

For n=1 write f_i S=hd M_1 and e-tilde_i T=soc e_i T. Adjunction realizes S in e_i(f_i S), so the simple-socle result gives e-tilde_i f_i S=S, with shifts restored. Conversely if S=soc e_i T, adjunction gives T as a simple quotient of Ind(S,L_1), hence T=f_i S. These are actual partial inverses. The raising operator decreases epsilon by1; lowering increases it by1. Iterating partial inverses shows hd Ind(S,L_n)=f_i^n S: strip the maximum-tail head n times using the unique original10 recursion, or apply the same adjunction and uniqueness at each one-strand stage. All statements hold at the first end by the identical first-end Mackey and dot arguments.

## Exact cyclotomic criterion

Let J^Lambda be generated by x_1^lambda_i on every word beginning with i. It annihilates a simple S exactly when each first-i corner has first-dot index at most lambda_i. The preceding theorem proves that index is epsilon_i^L(S). Thus

    J^Lambda S=0 iff epsilon_i^L(S)<=lambda_i for every i.

If a generator is nonzero, simplicity makes J^Lambda S=S and the quotient projection vanishes. If every generator vanishes, projection is S. This proves the criterion over all fields and Q without citing the omitted proof of LV Proposition2.4. Since first strands are preserved by right restriction, raising preserves the cyclotomic subcategory. For right induction, its generic unique head either survives, in which case quotient induction has that same unique head, or dies, in which case the quotient induction is zero: any nonzero finite module has a simple quotient, and any such quotient of the original induction must be its unique head.

The maximal-epsilon composition factors of e_i S are precisely the same simple shift orbit as its head/socle: their maximal corner is a constituent of N tensor Res L_r, whose single simple type identifies them by the maximal-tail recursion. The nil-Hecke branching calculation gives their graded coefficient as a shift of [r]_i. This concerns the full composition part; the socle and head each have one copy. The proof uses no choice and no self-dual representative.

items.title: Minimal-parabolic diagrams have a faithful PBW and bubble normal form
items.statement: Fix a color $i$. In the formal graded minimal-parabolic proof category of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], the reduced perfect-matching diagrams, dot monomials on their open components, and monomials in the independent far-left normalized $i$-bubble coefficients form a basis of every morphism space. In particular, at all-downward boundaries of weight difference $\beta$, the morphism space is the corresponding KLR PBW corner tensored with the polynomial ring in one positive bubble family; the opposite/fake family is its coefficientwise reciprocal. The graded polynomial flag models of [[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]], with universal monic framing and arbitrarily large auxiliary framing at each fixed physical source weight, are jointly faithful. The assertion is about this formal proof category before cyclotomic quotient transfer.
items.strategy:
Use $\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for all colors. The formal category's relations are the exact model-verified local equations: downward KLR, both rank-one triangles, cyclic dots, rho/cross-and-cap equations and bubble inversion, mixed cap/cup equations, and the finite-coefficient bubble slides. For an $i$ root $x$, its normalized bubble series changes by $(1-xt)^{\pm2}$; for a spectator $j$ root $y$ it changes by $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)^{\pm1}$, where $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$ has constant coefficient $1$. These are verified directly because the model series is $p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2$, adjoining an $i$ root multiplies $c_r$ by $u-x$, and adjoining a spectator multiplies $p$ by $Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$. Every fixed inverse coefficient is a finite polynomial recursion. These slides are specified formal relations checked on the model; deriving a slide from the faithfulness being proved is not used.

To span, move dots to fixed component positions with cyclicity and KLR dot moves. An equal-color correction has one fewer crossing. Sort each $i$ cup/cap toward a boundary or the far-left closed-component position using the specified mate equations. A main term passes one of its finitely many crossing obstacles; a correction term removes an unsorted open-component extremum or such an obstacle. Rank-one cross-and-cap sums are finite: open dot counts are nonnegative and negative-degree bubbles vanish, bounding the indices at a fixed total degree. Adjacent opposed cup/cap pairs cancel by the triangles. Induct on the lexicographic pair of unsorted extrema and remaining crossing obstacles, and on crossing length for correction terms. Closed components have color $i$; cancel extra extrema, slide them left by the finite coefficient equations, and express the reverse family by bubble inversion. Coxeter deletion and KLR braid/quadratic straightening then reduce each open matching to the selected reduced diagram, with all braid defects shorter. This yields the stated finite span. At all-downward boundaries every open arc joins bottom to top, hence is a colored permutation; the reduced matching and its dots are exactly a PBW monomial. For general boundaries the two triangles give invertible Hom correspondences bending the upward $i$ endpoints to the other boundary, and the same straightening has unit leading matching coefficients.

For independence hold the physical source weight $\mu$ fixed and write $\mu_i=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$. Choose fixed nonnegative spectator background counts $m_j$ and let $A_{\rm spect}=\sum_{j\ne i}(-a_{ij})m_j$. For an increasing background $i$ count $r$, set $N=\mu_i+2r$ and $\lambda_i=N-A_{\rm spect}$. These equations keep the physical weight $N-2r=\mu_i$ fixed. Only $i$ dominance is needed, since the model has no spectator upward generator; one may take all $m_j=0$. Use the universal graded monic framing $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}+z_1u^{\lambda_i-1}+\cdots+z_{\lambda_i}$ with independent $\deg z_a=2d_i a$. Put $p=a_i\prod Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $c_r=\prod(u-x_a)$. The correct normalized series is $\mathcal B(t)=p^{\rm rev}/(c_r^{\rm rev})^2=a_i^{\rm rev}U(t)$, $U_0=1$. Its coefficient $\mathcal B_a=z_a+\sum_{1\le\ell<a}z_\ell U_{a-\ell}+U_a$ is unit triangular in the framing variables. The reciprocal family's coefficient is $-z_a$ plus lower framing indices. Thus the first $D$ bubble coefficients are independent whenever $\lambda_i\ge D$, even in characteristic two and at negative physical weight. No claim of a unit old-root coefficient is made: $\mathcal B_1=p_1+2e_1$ can lose its root term in characteristic two.

A nonzero finite PBW/bubble combination remains nonzero after that triangular substitution over the independent polynomial coefficient domain. The generic KLR polynomial representation has a distinct nonzero leading permutation for each selected crossing word; choose a polynomial test vector with nonzero output, clearing a finite denominator if needed. Let $D$ bound the bubble indices and let $B$ bound the actual internal degrees of that vector and its output; both are finite and are determined in the untruncated polynomial ring. Let $L$ bound the number of added $i$ flags in the tested words. Every monic flag relation and factor-ring coefficient relation after those flags has degree at least $2d_i(N-r-L+1)=2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)$; spectator appends can only increase $N$. All coefficient and root variables are nonnegatively graded and all dot degrees are positive. Choose $r\ge0$, $\lambda_i\ge D$, and $2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)>B$, also making any finitely required background root count large enough. Such an integer exists while $\mu$ is fixed. The ideal generated by the homogeneous model relations cannot meet degrees at most $B$, so the nonzero PBW output survives in that flag model. This is exact degree separation, not a deformation-flatness inference. The model's ordered word shifts, $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$ with $i$ last, make every crossing homogeneous of degree $-b_{jk}$; the polynomial witness is checked before its overall word shift. The formal upward generator is $H_i=E_i^{\rm basic}\{-d_i(1+h_{\rm input})\}$, not unnormalized restriction, so its spectator commutators are truly degree zero. Hence the faithful underlying witness is also a witness in the specified graded model.

The downward spanning map is therefore injective. The finite unit-triangular bending change then gives independence for the full matching family. Specializing the far-left bubble variables acts only on that tensor factor in the downward normal form; no ordinary KLR relation appears from coefficient evaluation alone. items.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be dominant, $\lambda_j=\langle h_j,\Lambda\rangle$, and let $\mathcal P_i$ be [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], with its homogeneous polynomial realization and PBW/bubble normal form. Fix monic $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}+\sum_{r<\lambda_j}c_{j,r}u^r$. For the standard graded cyclotomic quotient take $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$ as in [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]. More generally first take universal graded coefficients of degree $2d_j(\lambda_j-r)$; arbitrary monic specializations over the field are interpreted as ungraded.

In the representable category $\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)$, let $J$ be the ideal generated by $1_{H_iv_\Lambda}$ and $a_j(x)1_{G_jv_\Lambda}$ for every $j$, closed under arbitrary vertical pre/postcomposition and horizontal whiskering by the allowed 1-morphisms. For downward words $\mu,\nu$ of the same weight $\beta$, include their ordinary KLR corner by the PBW/bubble normal form. Then
$$J\cap e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\mu)=e(\nu)I_a(\beta)e(\mu),\qquad I_a(\beta)=\sum_j R(\beta)a_j(x_1)e(j,\beta-\alpha_j)R(\beta).$$
The vacuum bubble specialization is forced by these generators: $A_\Lambda(t)=1+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}t+\cdots+c_{i,0}t^{\lambda_i}$ and $\mathsf H_\Lambda=A_\Lambda^{-1}$. Consequently the map from the ordinary monic cyclotomic corner to the downward-word Hom corner of $\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)/J$ is an isomorphism, with composition corresponding to multiplication. This holds over every degree-zero field for the entire admissible homogeneous $Q$ family, without finite-type or characteristic-zero restrictions. Inhomogeneous monic specializations assert the ungraded corner equality, not a graded quantum-action conclusion.
items.strategy:
Use [[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]] for the formal graded maps, both triangles, rho inverse blocks, mixed dot compatibility, cross-and-cap identities and normalized bubble slides, and [[lem-minimal-parabolic-diagrams-have-pbw-bubble-normal-form]] for the complete matching normal form and the downward PBW tensor independent vacuum bubbles. The formal $H_i$ is normalized projective restriction with input shift $-d_i(1+h)$ in the model; it is distinct from raw basic restriction. These are mathematical suppliers, not a citation-only import. Apply the following finite argument before transporting any formal relation to the actual cyclotomic action.

## Vacuum coefficients: the specialization is forced, not an extra assumption

Use the trace packet's normalized cups/caps; let h_l be the bubble closed with lambda_i-1+l dots and extend negative-dot symbols by formal inversion. The formal rank-one identities give h_l=0 for l<0 and h_0=1. Close a_i(x)x^{l-1}=0 for l>=1. The exponent l-1 is nonnegative, so this is a lawful defining-ideal consequence, including when some resulting indices are negative. It gives

$$h_l+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}h_{l-1}+\cdots+c_{i,0}h_{l-\lambda_i}=0.$$

Thus H(t)=sum_{l>=0} h_l t^l is the inverse of a_i^{rev}(t)=1+c_{i,lambda_i-1}t+...+c_{i,0}t^{lambda_i}. Bubble inversion determines the opposite family A(t)=H(t)^{-1}=a_i^{rev}(t). Consequently Phi_i(u)=u^{lambda_i}A(u^{-1})=a_i(u). Each coefficient conclusion uses only a finite recurrence. The local polynomial-model supplier proves these rank-one identities; no faithful cyclotomic action or generic Frobenius theorem is used.

Distinguish the index from the literal dot count. An actual vacancy loop with r>=0 dots has A index lambda_i+1+r; it vanishes because A is a polynomial of degree at most lambda_i. The A coefficients with index 1,...,lambda_i are fake bubbles of negative dot count; in the monic branch they are prescribed coefficients, not zero. The opposite H family is generally an infinite reciprocal series. For a_i=u(u-1), A=1-t and H=(1-t)^{-1}. Setting all positive bubbles in both orientations to zero would wrongly change this deformation. In the standard branch both positive coefficient families vanish. If lambda_i=0, a_i=1 kills F_i v and A=H=1; the degree-zero fake coefficient remains 1.

Write S for this vacuum bubble coefficient specialization. By the recurrence S is already contained in J. By [[lem-minimal-parabolic-diagrams-have-pbw-bubble-normal-form]], specializing these central vacuum coefficients alone gives the all-downward corner R(beta), with no relations in its ordinary polynomial/crossing part. This uses the tensor-product normal form, not a flatness assertion. We can calculate in P_i/S and then include the E_i and first-strand generators.

## Bringing every bubble coefficient to the vacuum

After bending, a coefficient may initially be a bubble at source Lambda+alpha_i, immediately to the left of an added first i strand with dot z. It may not be replaced directly by the Lambda vacuum value. The required rank-one bubble-slide equation in coefficient normalization is

$$A_{\Lambda+\alpha_i}(t)=(1-zt)^2A_\Lambda(t),\qquad H_{\Lambda+\alpha_i}(t)=(1-zt)^{-2}H_\Lambda(t).$$

The weight indices differ by 2; these are normalized power series with constant coefficient 1. For each fixed coefficient this is a finite polynomial equation in z and the vacuum coefficients. Negative exponents on (1-zt) denote formal coefficient recursion, not inversion of z or an analytic infinite sum.

Here is an algebraic verification, independent of quotient faithfulness. In the unquotiented rank-one polynomial flag model, with total monic polynomial p and existing-root factor c_r, the normalized bubble series is p^{rev}/(c_r^{rev})^2; this is the coefficient/cap identity for the two monic flag pairings (equivalently complement factor divided by root factor). Adding the distinguished root z replaces c_r^{rev} by c_r^{rev}(1-zt). The target series is therefore the source series divided by (1-zt)^2. Multiplying proves the displayed equation; inversion gives the H equation. These finite coefficient equalities are explicit relations in the definition of the formal proof category and are verified by the local polynomial-model supplier. They are not derived from the normal-form faithfulness theorem that subsequently uses them for spanning. This uses only monic polynomial multiplication and coefficient inversion before quotienting, and does not claim that faithfulness survives a quotient.

Thus a finite diagram has, after finitely many coefficient slides, only polynomial dots on the added strand and bubble coefficients at Lambda. In P_i/S these coefficients are scalars. No source-weight bubble specialization or collision of two distinguished roots is assumed.

## The actual local straight and curl calculations

Use the actual rank-one cross-and-cap equations and their finite polynomial verification in the local model supplier; the same equations appear in Webster Figure2. The following dot-index calculation types the contraction directly and requires no two-root-collision identification.

The straight closure of the added leftmost i strand with r dots is the actual vacancy loop, with A index lambda_i+1+r. It is zero in P_i/S. This remains true for any polynomial dots with coefficients on the neighboring original strand, by linearity and dot cyclicity.

For the leftward single-crossing curl, Figure 2 expands it as a signed sum of a dotted uncrossed cap and a far-left bubble, with dot indices a+b=-1 and a>=0. Put b=-lambda_i-1+m. The bubble coefficient is A_m, and a=lambda_i-m. Terms with m<0 have negative bubble degree and vanish; terms with m>lambda_i have negative dots on the open strand and vanish. Therefore the undotted local curl is

$$\epsilon\sum_{m=0}^{\lambda_i}A_m x^{\lambda_i-m}=\epsilon a_i(x),\qquad \epsilon\in\{1,-1\}.$$

The sign is the fixed orientation/source-crossing unit. Since the statement is ideal membership, its value is immaterial; no unsigned equality of canonical maps is claimed. In characteristic 2 it is still a unit. When lambda_i=0 the sum is epsilon times the identity, matching a_i=1.

Let C(P) be this crossed closure with polynomial dots P(u,x), u on the added first strand and x on the first physical strand. The source nil-Hecke relation is kappa_1 u = x kappa_1 -1; natively tau_1 u = x tau_1 +1. Moving a u dot through the unique crossing gives

$$C(uP)=xC(P)+\epsilon' B(P),$$

where B(P) is a straight closure and epsilon' is the corresponding sign. All B(P)=0 by the preceding paragraph. Dots on the physical strand pull out by cyclicity. Induction on the two nonnegative dot exponents and linearity give

$$C(P)=\epsilon a_i(x)P(x,x).$$

This is the typed local calculation for arbitrary polynomial dots. It also equals epsilon times the coefficient of u^{-1} in a_i(u)P(u,x)/(u-x); the residue notation is a convenient finite coefficient identity, not an additional model identification. Spectator Q factors only change P or the exterior word morphisms; no factorization or specialization of Q is made.

## Bending every E_i-vacuum factor and the complete PBW split

An arbitrary generator summand factoring through A E_i v has maps f:F_mu v -> A E_i v and g:A E_i v -> F_nu v. The two specified adjunctions bend its vacuum E_i boundary. They yield f^flat:F_mu F_i(Lambda+alpha_i) -> A and g^sharp:A -> F_nu F_i(Lambda+alpha_i), with the prescribed shifts. The composite a=g^sharp f^flat has all-downward boundaries with one extra **first** i strand. Closing that added strand with the same cups/caps recovers gf by the adjunction triangles. This is a typed bend of the factor maps, not a claim that the internal word A is downward.

Apply [[lem-minimal-parabolic-diagrams-have-pbw-bubble-normal-form]] to a, straightening all its internal cups/caps into the matching/dot/far-left-bubble normal form. With all-downward boundaries, each open component connects bottom to top; their matching is a permutation. The result is a finite sum of downward PBW terms with bubble coefficients. Slide the coefficients across the first added strand as above and specialize S.

Let W=S_{n+1} and W_P be the subgroup permuting positions 2,...,n+1. There are exactly two W_P double cosets: W_P and W_P s_1 W_P. In the first, w fixes position 1. In the second, choose the minimal parabolic coset representatives that move the departing first strand to position 2 and the arriving strand from position 2; then complete with a permutation of the last n positions. This gives w=u s_1 v, u,v in W_P, with lengths adding. The resulting reduced word contains s_1 exactly once. Equivalently the two cosets record whether the distinguished first input is matched to the distinguished first output; the second coset's remaining matching is an arbitrary permutation after those distinguished endpoints are removed. The standard insertion/removal reduced-word construction proves length additivity. These are **double** cosets; merely choosing right cosets is insufficient.

Choose precisely these reduced words in PBW. Every term is either a word using crossings kappa_2,...,kappa_n only, or L kappa_1 M with both exterior crossing words using only those crossings and arbitrary polynomial dots. Reduced-word replacement errors have fewer crossings and polynomial coefficients, so PBW straightening terminates in this same finite family. Bubble and dot coefficients never require inverting a dot or Q.

In the first case the last n strands pull past the first cup/cap, leaving a straight vacancy loop; its value is zero. In the second, the first endpoint has color i at both boundaries. L and M fix position 1, so the color at position 2 immediately at the sole kappa_1 must also be i: otherwise the first output color would differ from i. This proves that the sole boundary crossing is equal-color. No unlike-color cap-off case has been omitted. Exterior L,M act on only the physical n strands and pull through the left closure by horizontal functoriality; polynomial dots on the two crossing strands are exactly the P already calculated. The local result is epsilon a_i(x_1)P(x_1,x_1) on the first physical i strand. Hence the total term lies in

$$R(\beta)a_i(x_1)e(i,\beta-\alpha_i)R(\beta).$$

Consequently **every** E_i-vacuum ideal summand, with arbitrary internal word A and arbitrary factor maps, has its downward value in the ordinary first-strand i ideal. This is the finite completeness statement missing from a merely faithful generic model. For n=0 there is only the straight case, so it imposes no vacuum scalar relation.

## Why arbitrary whiskers of the other monic generators add no relations

It is necessary to handle A a_j(x) id(F_j v) when A itself contains E_i; cap-off of unmarked E_i-vacuum factors alone does not establish this. The following finite normalization supplies that check.

First, in P_i/S modulo the E_i-vacuum ideal, the rank-one rho at dominant vacuum decomposes E_i F_i v as lambda_i shifted identity summands; the F_i E_i summand is zero. The dotted cup columns v_r, r=0,...,lambda_i-1, are a basis of these summands after the finite triangular adjustment determined by the inverse bubble coefficients. In that basis dot multiplication x is the companion matrix of a_i:

$$xv_r=v_{r+1}\ (r<\lambda_i-1),\qquad xv_{\lambda_i-1}=-\sum_{r=0}^{\lambda_i-1}c_{i,r}v_r.$$

One can verify the last column without assuming a one-dimensional Hom: pair it with each of the explicit dual cap rows of rho^{-1}. A raw cap row with s additional dots pairs with a cup column x^r by h_{r+s-lambda_i+1}; hence pairing a_i(x) with that row gives the recurrence at l=s+1. The dual rows are finite triangular combinations of these raw rows, so their entries are precisely linear combinations of h_l+c_{i,lambda_i-1}h_{l-1}+...+c_{i,0}h_{l-lambda_i}, all zero by the vacuum recurrence. All the projections vanish; rho's already imposed inverse matrix says the column itself vanishes. The earlier columns follow by one added dot. Thus a_i(x)=0 on E_i F_i v. For lambda_i=0 the object is zero, so the statement is vacuous. This is finite matrix algebra over the coefficient ring, not a rank or flatness argument.

Now normalize A a_j(x) at the intermediate **word-object** level and at its endomorphism simultaneously. Select the chronologically earliest E_i in A and move it toward the initial F_j v through the shorter negative prefix. Different-color commutation is the formal mixed isomorphism, natural in its input. For a same-color pair at input weight mu, put h=<h_i,mu> and retain the actual shifts in the following maps. If h>=0, write the appropriate canonical rho isomorphism (or its specified inverse, according to the orientation of rho) as r_h:E_i F_i -> F_i E_i direct-sum D_h, where D_h is the finite sum of h shifted identity functors. Conjugating an input-induced endomorphism by r_h gives the F_i E_i branch and the identity branches. This is a functor decomposition, natural in that endomorphism.

If h<0, the actual rho isomorphism instead has direction

$$r_h:F_iE_i\longrightarrow E_iF_i\oplus D_{-h}.$$

It does **not** decompose E_i F_i as F_i E_i plus identities. Let j_E,p_E be the inclusion and projection of its E_i F_i summand and define the natural retract maps

$$\iota_h=r_h^{-1}j_E:E_iF_i\longrightarrow F_iE_i,\qquad \pi_h=p_Er_h:F_iE_i\longrightarrow E_iF_i,\qquad \pi_h\iota_h=1.$$

For every input endomorphism b, naturality of r_h and its inverse gives iota_h (E_i F_i)(b) = (F_i E_i)(b) iota_h and pi_h (F_i E_i)(b) = (E_i F_i)(b) pi_h. Consequently

$$(E_iF_i)(b)=\pi_h(F_iE_i)(b)\iota_h.$$

Whisker these inclusion/projection maps by the remaining outer word. An arbitrary vertically sandwiched marked term g (E_i F_i)(b) f is therefore exactly (g pi_h) (F_i E_i)(b) (iota_h f). This moves the retained E_i one place toward the vacuum without asserting a false negative-weight direct-sum decomposition. The extra cups/caps in iota_h and pi_h belong to the adapted factor maps, not to the intermediate word whose normalization is being measured.

In both signs the input endomorphism b is the initial a_j on F_j v, with the shorter downward prefix attached. Naturality ensures the marker stays on that initial first strand. Positive-weight identity branches remove the chosen E_i and retain the ordinary first-strand marker. The branch retaining E_i (including the negative-weight retract branch) moves it one position nearer the initial F_j. At that strand, if j!=i, mixed dot compatibility sends the marker to F_j a_j(x) E_i v, hence zero modulo the E_i-vacuum ideal. If j=i, the vacuum weight is lambda_i>=0: the F_i E_i summand vanishes, and the identity-summand companion calculation above kills a_i. This last use of the companion matrix occurs only at the dominant vacuum, never at a negative intermediate weight.

Continue with the E_i generators in the resulting intermediate word objects. The lexicographic measure is (number of E_i letters in that word object, number of initial downward letters between its chronologically earliest E_i and the vacuum). An identity branch lowers the first coordinate; a retained-E_i branch lowers the second. For the negative-weight case this is the word F_i E_i in the displayed retract factorization, not the syntactic number of cups/caps or upward segments inside iota_h, pi_h, f or g. Outer whiskering and vertical composition leave this interpretation unchanged. Each step has a finite number of branches, and each branch terminates because the measure is a pair of nonnegative integers. Once the intermediate word is downward, its arbitrary adapted factor maps have all-downward boundaries and are reduced by [[lem-minimal-parabolic-diagrams-have-pbw-bubble-normal-form]]'s formal normal form; their internal cups/caps do not restart the object-word induction. Therefore every horizontal whisker of an initial monic generator reduces to ordinary downward first-strand ideal insertions plus E_i-vacuum ideal summands. The latter were completely handled above. The equalities and retract maps are natural transformations and actual vertical factorizations, not equalities in K_0.

## Exact intersection

For f in the included downward R corner belonging to J, express f as a finite sum of vertically factored horizontal whiskers of the defining generators. Add S, which was already forced by J. The E_i summands have downward values in I_a by the typed bend, PBW two-double-coset split, and local curl calculation. The marked a_j summands have downward values in I_a by the finite marked normalization. Any S coefficient summands are zero after the tensor-product coefficient specialization. Thus the value of f in the specialized downward corner lies in I_a. Because the same specialization leaves every ordinary downward polynomial/crossing f unchanged, f belongs to I_a as an element of R. This is the required reverse inclusion. The forward inclusion follows directly from the initial a_j generators and downward whiskering/vertical composition. No quotient faithfulness, cyclotomic basis rank, generic symmetric/Frobenius theorem, or unproved intersection premise has entered this argument.
