items.title: The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator in a small cyclotomic weight
items.statement:
Take $I=\{i\}$ with $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, $d_i=1$, $q_i=q$, and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$, so that $\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle=2$ and the standard cyclotomic quotient has relations $x_1^2e(\nu)=0$. Then:
(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]/(x_1^2)$ with graded dimension $1+q^2$, and $R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)=0$ for $n\ge3$, so the functors on the nonzero weights are $F^\Lambda_i k=R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i k=0$.
(b) The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relation of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-sl-two-categorical-commutator]] at $\beta=0$, $\lambda=\Lambda$ (case $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle=2\ge0$) reads $q^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus \mathrm{Id}\oplus q^2\mathrm{Id}\cong E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$; on the vacuum it says $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i k\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$, which is exactly $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$.
(c) Consequently, with the normalized operators of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]], on $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda(0))]$: $E_iF_i[1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ and $F_iE_i[1_\Lambda]=0$, so $[E_i,F_i][1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ with $K_i[1_\Lambda]=q^2[1_\Lambda]$; on $[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda(0))]$ the same commutator identity holds: $F_i[k]=q^{-1}[k\oplus k\{2\}]$, $E_i$ lowers back, $F_iE_i[k]=0$, and $E_iF_i[k]=(q+q^{-1})[k]$. This is the mixed relation of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]] verified at the first nontrivial weight.
items.strategy: At $\lambda=2$ the rank-one nil-Hecke quotient calculation in [[ex-cyclotomic-klr-quotients-in-ranks-zero-one-and-two]] gives precisely the three nonzero blocks at roots $0,\alpha_i,2\alpha_i$, with higher blocks zero. Basic restriction of $F_i k=k[x]/x^2$ is the vector space $k\oplus k\{2\}$; restriction of the vacuum is zero. The actual categorical commutator at target weight $h=2$ has identity shifts $0,2$, so its vacuum evaluation is exactly this direct sum. Projective $E$ on input root $\alpha_i$ carries $q^{-1}$, yielding $q^{-1}(1+q^2)=q^{-1}+q$. The KK module $F$ from the vacuum also carries $q^{-1}$ while KK $E$ is raw, giving the same commutator. The canonical module action instead shifts $E$ and leaves $F$ raw, also giving the same result. All agree with $(q^2-q^{-2})/(q-q^{-1})$. The vanishing is the proved pure rank-one finite-string calculation, not a false propagation inference from a single higher-degree dot polynomial.

items.title: The projective-simple Cartan pairing in a small cyclotomic block
items.statement: For rank one $d_i=1$, $\lambda=2$, let $B_r=R^\Lambda(r\alpha_i)$. The normalized simples are $S_0=k$, $S_1=k$ with $x=0$, and $S_2=C\{-1\}$ of graded dimension $q^{-1}+q$, where $C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$. Their normalized projective covers are $P_0=k$, $P_1=k[x]/x^2$, $P_2=S_2$. Then $T(P_r,S_s)=\delta_{rs}$, with distinct roots paired by zero. Under the integral projective identification $P_0,P_1,P_2$ map to $v,Fv,F^{(2)}v$, respectively, while $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[P_2]$ maps to $F^2v$. In $G_0$ the correct regular classes are $[B_1]=(1+q^2)[S_1]$ and $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[S_2]$. The canonical restricted-dual map sends $S_r$ to the form-dual of the corresponding divided lower vector; it does not identify $B_1$ with $S_1$.
items.strategy: The preceding rank-one example supplies $B_1$ and the centered polynomial column for $B_2$. The first regular module has two composition factors $S_1,S_1\{2\}$, giving $1+q^2$. The second block is the endomorphism matrix algebra of the graded column $S_2$, so its regular left module is the column tensored with its graded vector dual: the latter has dimension $q+q^{-1}$, yielding the stated shifted-column decomposition in both groups. The normalized cover-to-head Hom space is $k$ in degree zero and there are no other simple types in a block; quotient-cover evaluation identifies its tensor pairing with this value. The divided-power idempotent identifies $P_2$ with the actual second divided induction, hence $[B_2]=[2]_q[P_2]$ and $F^2=[2]_qF^{(2)}$. This is a cover/simple pairing, not a Cartan matrix claimed to be all ones or a trace that removes a denominator. The integral and dual-module theorems give the stated two identifications.
